programs.name: Massachusetts Residential Renewable Energy Credit
eligibilitySummary: You must own or rent and occupy the Massachusetts property as your principal residence, and you cannot be another taxpayer’s dependent.
Qualifying renewable-energy property can include equipment that uses or transmits solar energy to heat, cool, provide hot water, or generate electricity for the residence.

The credit is the smaller of 15% of net qualifying expenditure or $1,000. Prior energy credits claimed for the same residence reduce that lifetime maximum, and excluded costs or other incentives can change the qualifying expenditure.
claimSteps: Keep itemized invoices and records of incentives used to determine the net qualifying expenditure.
Complete Massachusetts Schedule EC and enter credit code SLRWND on Schedule CMS.
Report the allowed credit on the applicable Massachusetts Form 1 line and retain the schedules with your return.
programs.description: A Massachusetts personal income-tax credit equal to 15% of net qualifying renewable-energy expenditure at an owner-occupied principal residence, capped at $1,000.

programs.name: Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit — Heat Pumps

annualCaps.description: Combined annual cap for qualifying heat pumps, heat-pump water heaters, and biomass stoves or boilers.

eligibilitySummary: Property had to be placed in service by December 31, 2025; this credit is closed for new 2026 projects.
The home had to be in the United States and used as a residence by the taxpayer.
The equipment had to meet the applicable highest non-advanced CEE efficiency tier and 2025 manufacturer-identification rules.
claimSteps: Keep the itemized invoice and manufacturer certification information.
Report the 2025 qualified-manufacturer identification number.
File IRS Form 5695 for tax year 2025.
programs.description: A closed federal nonrefundable tax credit equal to 30% of eligible heat-pump costs, subject to a $2,000 shared annual cap.

programs.name: Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit — Insulation

annualCaps.description: Overall annual cap shared with qualifying doors, windows, audits, and specified residential energy property.
Maximum insulation and air-sealing credit before applying the shared general cap.

eligibilitySummary: Materials had to be installed by December 31, 2025; this credit is closed for new 2026 projects.
The taxpayer had to own and use the U.S. home as their principal residence.
Eligible insulation and air-sealing materials had to meet the applicable IECC criteria.
claimSteps: Keep receipts and product documentation.
Calculate the shared section 25C annual limitation.
File IRS Form 5695 for tax year 2025.
programs.description: A closed federal nonrefundable tax credit equal to 30% of eligible insulation and air-sealing material costs, within the $1,200 general annual cap.

programs.name: Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit — Heat-Pump Water Heaters

annualCaps.description: Combined annual cap for qualifying heat pumps, heat-pump water heaters, and biomass stoves or boilers.

eligibilitySummary: The qualifying heat-pump water heater had to be placed in service by December 31, 2025.
The home had to be in the United States and used as a residence by the taxpayer.
Conventional gas, propane, and oil water heaters used a different $600-per-item limit and are not represented by this record.
claimSteps: Keep the itemized invoice and manufacturer certification information.
Report the 2025 qualified-manufacturer identification number.
File IRS Form 5695 for tax year 2025.
programs.description: A closed federal nonrefundable tax credit equal to 30% of eligible heat-pump water-heater costs, subject to the shared $2,000 annual cap.

programs.name: Residential Clean Energy Credit — Solar
eligibilitySummary: Installation had to be completed by December 31, 2025; this credit is closed for new 2026 installations.
New qualifying solar property had to be installed at a U.S. home used by the taxpayer.
The nonrefundable credit could be carried forward when it exceeded current-year tax liability.
claimSteps: Keep the contract, paid invoices, and commissioning documentation.
Subtract any purchase-price-adjustment rebates from eligible cost as required.
File IRS Form 5695 for tax year 2025.
programs.description: A closed federal nonrefundable tax credit for 30% of eligible residential solar costs, with unused credit generally eligible for carryforward.

programs.name: New Clean Vehicle Credit
eligibilitySummary: The vehicle had to be acquired by September 30, 2025; this credit is closed for later acquisitions.
Modified AGI could not exceed the filing-status cap in the delivery year or preceding year.
MSRP could not exceed $55,000 for a car or $80,000 for an SUV, pickup, or van.
Eligibility and the actual credit amount depended on the specific VIN and accepted seller report.
claimSteps: Retain the IRS-accepted time-of-sale report.
Confirm the credit amount for the specific VIN.
File Form 8936 even if the credit was transferred to a registered dealer at point of sale.
programs.description: A closed federal nonrefundable tax credit of up to $7,500 that could optionally be transferred to a registered dealer as a point-of-sale discount.

programs.name: Previously Owned Clean Vehicle Credit
eligibilitySummary: The vehicle had to be acquired from a licensed dealer by September 30, 2025; this credit is closed for later acquisitions.
The sale price, including dealer-imposed fees, could not exceed $25,000.
Modified AGI could not exceed the filing-status cap in the delivery year or preceding year.
The model year had to be at least two years earlier than the purchase year, and transfer-history restrictions applied.
claimSteps: Retain the IRS-accepted time-of-sale report from the licensed dealer.
Confirm the vehicle and transfer history qualify.
File Form 8936 even if the credit was transferred to the dealer at point of sale.
programs.description: A closed federal nonrefundable tax credit equal to 30% of an eligible used vehicle's sale price, capped at $4,000, with an optional point-of-sale transfer.

programs.name: New York Solar Energy System Equipment Credit
eligibilitySummary: The solar equipment must be installed and used at your principal residence in New York State.
A purchase, qualifying lease, or qualifying power-purchase agreement may be eligible; a power-purchase agreement must span at least ten years.
Electric-generating systems must satisfy applicable utility interconnection and net-metering requirements.
The credit is nonrefundable, but unused credit may be carried forward for up to five years.
claimSteps: Keep the contract, invoices, proof of payment, and utility interconnection or net-metering documentation.
Determine qualified expenditures after excluding costs that do not qualify under the Form IT-255 instructions.
Complete Form IT-255 and submit it with New York Form IT-201 or IT-203.
Carry any allowed unused balance forward as instructed for up to five years.
programs.description: A New York personal income-tax credit equal to 25% of qualified residential solar equipment expenditures, capped at $5,000.

programs.name: NYS Clean Heat — Central Hudson Heat Pump Water Heater
eligibilitySummary: You must be an active Central Hudson electric customer.
The heat pump water heater must meet current ENERGY STAR requirements and the program's electrical specifications.
The purchase must use an eligible participating channel; program funding and terms can change.
claimSteps: Confirm the exact model is eligible before purchase.
Use Central Hudson's participating retailer, distributor, or contractor channel.
Have the program discount applied through the eligible channel and keep the itemized receipt.
programs.description: A $1,250 NYS Clean Heat customer incentive for an eligible residential heat pump water heater in Central Hudson territory.
